integrity: The theorem uses previously known classification of finite-field forms and classical group orders. All numerical examples are proved algebraically and checked in stated finite cases. No claim of external certification or exhaustive novelty.
limitations: Equivalent statements in dihedral-subgroup and projective-involution literature may exist; no independent mathematical validation.
scientific_integrity: Theoretical arguments have self-review only, without independent audit; finite computations are exact checks of small dimensions, not universal proofs.
scientific_limitations: Only odd prime powers, actual matrix lifts that square to identity, and full or determinant-one linear/unitary/symplectic/orthogonal groups. Excludes characteristic two and Omega or spinor-norm subgroups. Finite checker cases are not the general proof.
title: Anticommuting involutions in finite classical groups: orbit types and dihedral subgroup counts
